from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Ellipse has two Dandelin spheres.",
            "Each touches the plane at a focus.",
            "Points on the ellipse follow distance rules.",
            "Distances to foci sum to a constant.",
            "This defines the ellipse perfectly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of Proof (Focus: Ellipse)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Ellipse and foci
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.0, height=2.0, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "B2", "E5")
        f1 = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(ellipse.get_center() + LEFT * 0.75)
        f2 = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(ellipse.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.75)
        self.add(ellipse, f1, f2)
        
        # Point P on ellipse
        p = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        p.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(0))
        
        l1 = Line(p.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color=BLUE)
        l2 = Line(p.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color=BLUE)
        
        # Text for sum
        sum_text = MathTex(r"d_1 + d_2 = \text{const}", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_text, "A1")

        def update_l1(m):
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), f1.get_center())
        def update_l2(m):
            m.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), f2.get_center())
        def update_p(m):
            t = self.time * 0.3
            p.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(t % 1))

        l1.add_updater(update_l1)
        l2.add_updater(update_l2)
        p.add_updater(update_p)
        self.add(l1, l2, p)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFCCCC"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(f1.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), f2.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#CCFFCC"))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#CCCCFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Expanding to Parabola and Hyperbola", [
            "Change the plane angle to shift shapes.",
            "Parabolas use one sphere tangent to plane.",
            "Hyperbolas require spheres in both cones."
        ])

        # Define mobjects
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=3, resolution=(10, 10)).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5+UP*0.5, LEFT*1.5+UP*0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW).set_fill(opacity=0.8)

        # Stage 1
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(cone, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(plane, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), Create(plane))
        self.play(plane.animate.rotate(0.5, about_point=self.grid['C3']))

        # Stage 2
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        
        # Stage 3
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        sphere2 = sphere.copy().move_to(self.grid['B4'])
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere2), cone.animate.rotate(0.2, axis=RIGHT))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections
outline.target_audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduates

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Cone and the Plane
sections.content: Briefly define a double-napped cone and a cutting plane. Establish that a conic section is the curve created where a plane intersects the cone.
sections.example: Imagine a flashlight beam hitting a wall; the shape of the light depends on the angle of the flashlight relative to the wall.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Dandelin Spheres'—spheres placed inside the cone such that they are tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point).
sections.example: Visualize two tennis balls tucked inside a party hat, wedged perfectly so they touch the inner surface of the hat and a flat sheet of glass cutting through it.

sections.title: The Geometry of Proof (Focus: Ellipse)
sections.content: Explain the 'Focal Property.' The points where the spheres touch the plane are the foci. For any point P on the ellipse, the distances to the two foci are related to the distances to the contact circles, effectively proving the definition of an ellipse.
sections.example: An ant walking along the rim of the ellipse; as it moves, the sum of its distances to the two 'contact points' remains constant, just like tying a string between two pins.

sections.title: Expanding to Parabola and Hyperbola
sections.content: Demonstrate how changing the angle of the cutting plane changes the number of spheres that can fit. A parabola requires one sphere tangent to the plane; a hyperbola requires spheres in both nappes.
sections.example: A satellite dish (parabola) uses one focus to gather signals, while a stylized hourglass shape represents the two-sided nature of the hyperbola.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude that Dandelin Spheres provide a bridge between the 3D geometry of the cone and the 2D algebraic equations of conic sections.
sections.example: Using a 3D animation tool, rotate the cutting plane to cycle through Circle -> Ellipse -> Parabola -> Hyperbola, highlighting how the spheres 'dance' to maintain tangency.
